newsitem.title: USA: Oregon taps State Street for investments.
newsitem.headline: Oregon taps State Street for investments.

text.p: Oregon state Treasurer Jim Hill said Wednesday he signed a contract to consolidate state Treasury investment operations under State Street Bank and Trust Co.
The investment funds managed by the state Treasury are expected to realize $21 million in savings as a result of the consolidation, Hill said in a statement.
State Street Bank and Trust Co is a wholly-owned subsidiary of State Street Boston Corp.

As the state Treasury's so-called custody bank, State Street is responsible for settling all trades and transactions for all funds managed by the Treasury, including the Public Employees Retirement Fund, which currently stands at $24 billion.
State Street will also provide financial reporting, maintain the safekeeping of all state securities, and perform investment accounting and income collection functions.
"This is a substantial and direct savings to the funds that we have under management," Hill said. "We are consolidating from three custodial banks to one."

This should result in a savings of approximately $3.3 million per year in custody fees alone, Hill said. In addition, the treasurer said he expects to increase the funds' earnings from securities lending.
Hill said State Street Bank was selected after his office evaluated major global custody banks in the market.
